study type: Case series with in vivo animal model
outcome: Exacerbated motor response to pentylenetetrazole (in zebrafish)
cohort: The study included nine human subjects from seven unrelated families harbouring homozygous loss-of-function ABCC9 variants, an eighth family with observed intra-uterine fetal death, and zebrafish used for in vivo studies.
finding: The study defined an ABCC9 loss-of-function-related phenotype, expanding the genotypic and phenotypic spectrum of ABCC9-related intellectual disability and myopathy syndrome (AIMS) and revealing novel human pathologies from KATP channel dysfunction.
